name: Question 5
problem:
A study has recorded and analyzed the results of the parliamentary elections of a particular country, held every four years. The study shows how voter preference changes from one political party to another. The table below shows the results of this study.

|  |  | From: |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  |  | **Yellow Party** | **Blue Party** | **Red Party** |
| To: | **Yellow Party** | $0.7$ | $0.1$ | $0.3$ |
| **Blue Party** | $0.2$ | $0.8$ | $0.3$ |  |
| **Red Party** | $0.1$ | $0.1$ | $0.4$ |  |

For example, $10%$ of the people who voted for the yellow party in the last election will vote for the red party in the next election.

If the electorate contains $5.6$ million voters and the given probabilities remain constant election after election, how many people will vote for the red party after many elections have taken place?
worked_solution:
From the table, we get the corresponding stochastic matrix 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}0.7 & 0.1 & 0.3 \\ 0.2 & 0.8 & 0.3 \\ 0.1 & 0.1 & 0.4\end{aligned}].
$$

Notice that the matrix $P$ contains only positive entries. So, the matrix $P$ is regular. 
As a result, after many elections, the distribution will eventually converge to the steady-state vector of $P,$ and this convergence does not depend on the initial state.

Recall that a steady-state vector of a stochastic matrix $P$ is a stochastic vector $q$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}Pq=q\,⟹\,(P-I)q=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing $P-I,$ we get

$$
P-I=[\begin{aligned}0.7 & 0.1 & 0.3 \\ 0.2 & 0.8 & 0.3 \\ 0.1 & 0.1 & 0.4\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-0.3 & 0.1 & 0.3 \\ 0.2 & -0.2 & 0.3 \\ 0.1 & 0.1 & -0.6\end{aligned}].
$$

The matrix equation $(P-I)q=0$ is equivalent to the system of linear equations with the augmented matrix $M,$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-0.3 & 0.1 & 0.3 & 0 \\ 0.2 & -0.2 & 0.3 & 0 \\ 0.1 & 0.1 & -0.6 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:=10{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{2}:=10{R}_{2} \\ {R}_{3}:=10{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 & 3 & 0 \\ 2 & -2 & 3 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & -6 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}↔{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -6 & 0 \\ 2 & -2 & 3 & 0 \\ -3 & 1 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+3{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -6 & 0 \\ 0 & -4 & 15 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & -15 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -6 & 0 \\ 0 & -4 & 15 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has two pivot columns (the $1$st and $2$nd). Thus, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain 

$$
{x}_{2}=\frac{15}{4}{x}_{3}.
$$

 
Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

$$
{x}_{1}+\frac{15}{4}{x}_{3}-6{x}_{3}=0\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=\frac{9}{4}{x}_{3}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{9}{4}{x}_{3} \\ \frac{15}{4}{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Since the steady-state vector must be stochastic, its entries should add up to $1.$ Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{9}{4}{x}_{3}+\frac{15}{4}{x}_{3}+{x}_{3} & =1 \\ 7{x}_{3} & =1 \\ {x}_{3} & =\frac{1}{7}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
q=[\begin{aligned}\frac{9}{28} \\ \frac{15}{28} \\ \frac{1}{7}\end{aligned}].
$$

So, after many elections, $\frac{1}{7}$ of the people will vote for the red party. Therefore, the number of people that will vote for the red party equals

$$
\frac{1}{7}\cdot 5.6\,\text{million}=0.8\,\text{million}.
$$

html:
Question 5
?

A study has recorded and analyzed the results of the parliamentary elections of a particular country, held every four years. The study shows how voter preference changes from one political party to another. The table below shows the results of this study.

From:
Yellow Party Blue Party Red Party
To: Yellow Party 0.7 0.1 0.3
Blue Party 0.2 0.8 0.3
Red Party 0.1 0.1 0.4

For example, 10% of the people who voted for the yellow party in the last election will vote for the red party in the next election.

If the electorate contains 5.6 million voters and the given probabilities remain constant election after election, how many people will vote for the red party after many elections have taken place?

a
1.2 million
b
1 million
c
0.9 million
d
1.6 million
e
0.8 million
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

From the table, we get the corresponding stochastic matrix P=[0.70.10.30.20.80.30.10.10.4].

Notice that the matrix P contains only positive entries. So, the matrix P is regular. As a result, after many elections, the distribution will eventually converge to the steady-state vector of P, and this convergence does not depend on the initial state.

Recall that a steady-state vector of a stochastic matrix P is a stochastic vector q such that

Pq=q⟹(P−I)q=0.

Computing P−I, we get

P−I=[0.70.10.30.20.80.30.10.10.4]−[100010001]=[−0.30.10.30.2−0.20.30.10.1−0.6].

The matrix equation (P−I)q=0 is equivalent to the system of linear equations with the augmented matrix M, which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination as follows:

M=[−0.30.10.300.2−0.20.300.10.1−0.60]R1:=10R1R2:=10R2R3:=10R3∼[−31302−23011−60]R3↔R1∼[11−602−230−3130]R2:=R2−2R1R3:=R3+3R1∼[11−600−415004−150]R3:=R3+R2∼[11−600−41500000]

The reduced matrix above has two pivot columns (the 1st and 2nd). Thus, x3 is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain x2=154x3. Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain x1+154x3−6x3=0⟹x1=94x3.

Hence, the general solution is [94x3154x3x3],x3∈R.

Since the steady-state vector must be stochastic, its entries should add up to 1. Therefore, we have 94x3+154x3+x3=17x3=1x3=17.

Therefore, q=[928152817].

So, after many elections, 17 of the people will vote for the red party. Therefore, the number of people that will vote for the red party equals 17⋅5.6million=0.8million.
